Three four-process metadata-write bursts (one warmup plus two further rounds). Barrier confirms all managers loaded before revocation; later stale writes retain that revocation and all four additions.
limits: Local cooperating POSIX filesystem only. Operations explicitly reject unsupported platforms; import of signing helpers remains available.
No physical power-cut test. Fsync failure after publication propagates an error but may leave the complete new inode/metadata visible; this is not rollback.

Keyring and metadata are separate stores, not a crash-atomic transaction. Existing in-memory fallback is not durable private-key storage; a replacement key mismatched with old metadata is not returned.
No protection against a malicious same-UID process replacing private directories or advisory lock files; all legitimate store users must follow the locking protocol.
Revocation blocks this API; previously copied private material is not erased.
Existing hardcoded sealer passphrase remains outside these three findings; no confidentiality or hardware-attestation certification.
